name: Panoxyl

card.summary: A benzoyl peroxide acne wash and gel brand that kills acne bacteria and clears pimples to give clearer skin.
card.note: Can cause dryness, irritation, and can bleach fabrics and hair.

quick.overview:
PanOxyl is a brand of benzoyl peroxide, a long-standing over-the-counter acne ingredient sold as washes and gels. Benzoyl peroxide kills Cutibacterium acnes bacteria, unclogs pores and may reduce inflammation, so the visible payoff is fewer pimples and clearer-looking skin.

Trials from the 1970s onward have tested PanOxyl gels: a 1986 randomised study reported at least a 50% drop in lesions in over 80% of 48 patients with a 5% benzoyl peroxide product over eight weeks, and a 2003 trial used PanOxyl 4% gel as the comparator.
quick.how: People use it as a facial or body wash or a leave-on gel, usually in 2.5% to 10% strengths, and it is often combined with a retinoid such as adapalene or with antibiotics in acne routines. Results are generally assessed over weeks.
quick.risks: Redness, burning and peeling are common and dose-dependent. It can permanently bleach fabrics, towels and hair. Hypersensitivity is rare.

lead: PanOxyl is a brand name for benzoyl peroxide products used for acne, alongside names such as Benzac [3]. Benzoyl peroxide reduces oil, unclogs pores and kills Cutibacterium acnes through free-radical activity, and acne products typically contain 2.5% to 10% [3]. For appearance, the goal is fewer inflamed pimples and clearer skin.

PanOxyl 5% gel was tested in a 1979 trial of 150 patients with Airol retinoic acid cream; the combination of morning retinoid and evening PanOxyl was judged most satisfactory [2]. In a 1986 randomised contralateral study of 48 patients, 5% alcohol-based PanOxyl and a water-based product performed equally, with more than 80% of patients getting at least a 50% reduction in lesions after eight weeks, and the water-based product caused less irritation [1].

Benzoyl peroxide's effect on oil is debated: a small study of ten men using PanOxyl-10 found no significant change in sebum secretion [4]. Mouse studies of the PanOxyl gel and tumour formation have also been published [5].

chain: Apply benzoyl peroxide wash or gel
Kills acne bacteria and unclogs pores
angle.text: Benzoyl peroxide directly targets the bacteria and clogged pores behind inflamed acne, so people use it to reduce breakouts. Clearer skin is the visible result.

infobox: Over the counter; also Rx combinations

paras: Acne treatment: lesions fall in studies of 5% PanOxyl, and it is paired with retinoids in some regimens [1][2].

Benzoyl peroxide kills C. acnes, unclogs pores and may limit neutrophil reactive-oxygen release [3]. A study of PanOxyl-10 on forehead skin found no significant change in sebaceous gland secretion over six weeks [4].

Redness, burning and irritation are common and often ease with continued use; about 1 in 500 people are hypersensitive, and contact can bleach fabrics and hair [3]. In the 1986 trial the alcohol-based PanOxyl caused more irritation than a water-based comparator [1]. Mouse work on PanOxyl gel and UV or chemical carcinogenesis reported mixed results [5], and an IARC review in 1999 found no convincing link to skin cancer in humans [3].

The 1986 randomised study (48 patients) found no difference in effect between 5% water-based and alcohol-based PanOxyl [1]. A 1979 trial of 150 patients found PanOxyl plus Airol superior to either alone [2]. A 2003 trial of 60 patients compared a stabilised hydrogen peroxide cream with PanOxyl 4% gel [6]. A 2005 UK trial of 649 patients compared five antimicrobial regimens for facial acne [7].

timeline.event: Benzoyl peroxide first prepared by Benjamin Collins Brodie [3].
Approved in the US for acne [3].
